summary: Every element of the causal chain that produced the five largest mass extinctions of the last half-billion years is presently accelerating in the Earth system. The rate of the modern perturbation exceeds every peer-reviewed paleoclimate reference case. A six-intervention portfolio, deployed together at wartime industrial scale beginning now, is the physically necessary and sufficient response. The window in which that portfolio remains fully effective closes between 2028 and 2040. The anthropogenic-versus-feedback tipping point is expected between 2035 and 2040; corrected for the at-least-order-of-magnitude higher rate of contemporary carbon release, loss of agency — the point at which coordinated intervention can no longer arrest the cascade — arrives 200 to 400 years after feedback engagement under sustained portfolio deployment, and collapses onto the tipping point itself under any scenario in which the portfolio is not deployed within the 2028–2040 window. Background. The five largest mass-extinction events of the Phanerozoic share a consistent causal chain: rapid carbon injection to the ocean-atmosphere system, followed by warming, ocean deoxygenation, acidification, and preferential loss of marine calcifiers, with multi-million-year recovery for reef ecosystems. Every element of that chain is presently active and gaining speed. The current anthropogenic perturbation is capable of driving a combination and magnitude of ocean geochemical changes unparalleled in the geological record reviewed by Hönisch et al. (2012), which covers approximately the past 300 million years. The reef–ocean-oxygen–land coupling documented in the End-Permian record demonstrates that marine biosphere collapse propagates to terrestrial extinction through the shared oxygen and biogeochemical infrastructure of the coupled Earth system; contemporary marine indicators are therefore leading indicators of terrestrial as well as marine risk. Approach. This three-part synthesis compiles peer-reviewed reconstructions of the Big Five causal chain, measures each element against the contemporary Earth system using the most recent authoritative data (Friedlingstein et al. 2026; Wu et al. 2021; Zeebe et al. 2016; Hönisch et al. 2012; Schmidtko et al. 2017; Eddy et al. 2021; Spady et al. 2026), specifies the physically necessary intervention portfolio, and characterizes the near-term feedback, resource, and civilizational risk environment those interventions must succeed in. Part I establishes the paleoclimate analog. Part II specifies the intervention portfolio. Part III maps the contemporary Earth system the Part II portfolio must succeed in — which climate feedbacks are already engaged and how they cascade, which physical resources are hitting hard limits inside the same two-to-three-decade window, and how those pressures translate into food, water, migration, health, economic, and governance strain — and closes with the North American Climate Pain Scale (NAPS), a 1–10 diagnostic instrument that anchors climate severity to concrete events so policymakers and the public can locate today's conditions and the trajectory ahead. Findings. Every element of the paleoclimate extinction causal chain is presently active. Atmospheric CO₂ (422.8 ppm, 2024 global annual mean; Friedlingstein et al. 2026) has exceeded the reconstructed latest-Permian baseline of 426 (+133 / −96) ppm (Wu et al. 2021, Nature Communications). The rate of contemporary carbon release is at least an order of magnitude above the sustained maximum Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum rate (Zeebe, Ridgwell and Zachos 2016, Nature Geoscience). Ocean acidification is proceeding at roughly ten times the PETM rate (Hönisch et al. 2012, Science). The global ocean has lost 4.8 ± 2.1 petamoles of dissolved oxygen since 1960 (Schmidtko, Stramma and Visbeck 2017, Nature). Global living coral cover has declined approximately 50 percent since 1957 (Eddy et al. 2021, One Earth), with cumulative satellite reef-
title: Inside the Extinction Envelope: A Systemic Review and Meta-Analysis of Paleoclimate Extinction Markers with Comments on the Necessary Array of Last-Threshold Interventions

summary: Climate change affects human well-being through interacting physical, ecological, infrastructural, and socioeconomic processes rather than through a single exposure or disease pathway. Major assessments identify observed harms to health, food and water security, livelihoods, settlements, and ecosystems, alongside increasing risks with additional warming (IPCC, 2022a). This narrative review develops a cross-sector framework from a source inventory of 154 human-impact pathways in 14 domains, supported by major assessments, selected peer-reviewed studies, and institutional datasets. Literature selection used targeted web-index searches and source verification through 2 October 2026; the review does not estimate pooled effects or claim exhaustive systematic coverage. The synthesis distinguishes direct injury and illness, ecosystem-mediated harms, failures of essential services, financial transmission, and losses of social and cultural continuity. Representative quantitative findings illustrate substantial existing burdens, but attribution studies, ecological associations, exposure models, displacement records, and conditional forecasts measure different quantities and cannot be combined into a universal five-year trajectory (Vicedo-Cabrera et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2026; Clement et al., 2021). Compound hazards and service interdependencies can increase losses beyond the directly affected sector, while repeated shocks can reduce the capacity to recover or adapt (Zscheischler et al., 2018; IPCC, 2023). A reporting framework is proposed that records the outcome, population, baseline, geography, time horizon, emissions and development assumptions, adaptation, and uncertainty for each indicator. The central contribution is an integrated interpretation and measurement architecture, not a new forecast of global mortality, migration, or societal collapse. Effective assessment should preserve evidence of serious and interacting harms without converting uncertain thresholds or heterogeneous studies into unsupported calendar-specific predictions.
title: Climate change impacts humans: A cross-sector narrative review of impact pathways, cascading risks, and accountable quantification

summary: Reconstructing Earth's deep-time paleoclimate record provides a critical framework for evaluating modern anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we synthesize proxy records from the "Big Five" mass extinction events—Late Ordovician (LOME), Late Devonian, Permian-Triassic (PTME), Triassic-Jurassic (TJME), and Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg)—and evaluate their proxy signals against modern biogeochemical trends. While cumulative carbon emissions during deep-time hyperthermals were larger in absolute magnitude, current annual carbon injection rates ( ∼ 10 G t C / y e a r ) and global warming velocities ( ∼ 0.2° C / d e c a d e ) exceed reconstructed pre-extinction baselines by factors of 10x to 100x. We catalog 17 positive climate feedback loops, 16 of which are currently active, and apply an Earth System Feedback Framework to demonstrate that integrating biogeochemical and cryospheric tipping dynamics elevates standard Equilibrium Climate Sensitivity ( E C S ≈ 3.0° C ) to an Earth System Sensitivity gain factor of G E S S ≈ 4.76 ( E S S ≈ 4.0–5.0° C for doubled C O 2 ). Synthesizing this feedback framework with Earth system tipping point literature (e.g., Armstrong McKay et al., 2022; Steffen et al., 2018; Kemp et al., 2022), we use this feedback gain function to model the boundary and evaluate the risk horizon for reaching a "Point of Human Agency Loss"—defined as the biogeochemical threshold where autonomous natural feedback emissions ( ≥ 10.0 G t C O 2 e / y e a r ) match or exceed maximum technological human mitigation and carbon removal capacity. We establish that crossing the 1.5° C to 2.0° C global warming horizon (projected mid-century) shifts the Earth system into a self-sustaining feedback regime. Driven by coupled biophysical stress vectors (niche thermal limits, crop yield collapses, and hydrological contraction; Xu et al., 2020) and the non-linear carrying-capacity decay function K ( T ) , human support capacity is projected to contract non-linearly from baseline Holocene levels ( ∼ 8.5–9.0 b i l l i o n ) to an equilibrium ceiling of ∼ 1.3–1.5 b i l l i o n at a stabilized state ( +3.3–3.5° C ). Finally, we perform a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) across 16 proposed climate interventions, evaluating scale, cost, geopolitical friction, termination shock, and moral hazard risk. We conclude that while physical variables (temperature, ocean pH) may be geochemically reversible over centuries via solar radiation management and permanent carbon removal, biospheric destruction, species extinction, and sea-level commitment exhibit severe hysteresis (path-dependence where a system fails to return to its initial state even if forcing is removed), making damage containment rather than ecosystem restoration the primary operational objective.
title: Climate forcing, positive feedbacks, and planetary tipping points: A synthesis of deep-time proxies, earth system sensitivity, and interventional feasibility

summary: Shincheonji Church of Jesus (commonly Shincheonji) is a new Christian millenarian church established in 1984 by Lee Man-hee (b. 1931) in South Korea. Shincheonji is an abbreviation of the phrase sincheongukjigu (신천국지구) which translates to 'New Heaven New Earth,' a reference to Revelation 21:1. Shincheonji can also be classified as a grassroots Korean religious movement or form of Christianity due to its development in South Korea, its close connections to earlier Korean millenarian Christian movements, and the they understand the South Korean nation as the location in which the prophecies contained Revelation have been fulfilled. Although South Korea is home to more members of Shincheonji than any other country, it is an international church with members and locations across Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Oceania. This entry, however, is focused on the Korean context. While the church has always been the subject of mass media attention and public scrutiny in South Korea, it gained the attention of international news media in February 2020 when a Covid-19 cluster infection in the city of Daegu was traced to one of its members. Shincheonji is often labelled as 'idan' (or 'heresy') or saibi jonggyo (which can be translated to 'pseudo-religion') by critical and 'anti-cult' Protestant theologians and pastors we well as in mainstream news and entertainment media. Shincheonji teachings that the prophecies of Revelations have already been fulfilled in South Korea in the 20th century, with the founder, Lee Man-hee (or Chairman Lee to members) as the witness these events. Although Christ's second coming is yet to occur, Shincheonji teaches that the old heaven and earth will give way to the new heaven and the new earth (which is Shincheonji). The 144,000 elect will dwell in the millennial kingdom: the holy city of the new Jerusalem. To bring about the Second Coming, it is understood that humans must work with God to create a peaceful world that mirrors heaven. While this entry attempts to outline key features, beliefs, and practices within Shincheonji as well as their social, cultural, and political engagements, this is complicated by Shincheonji's strategies of knowledge protection and information management. As a marginalised and minority religious community within South Korea, members can face harsh social, economic, and physical consequences should their faith commitments be revealed. As a result, Shincheonji is very careful about sharing information due to fears of negative public perceptions. Shincheonji also believes that knowledge of biblical truth offers salvation and eternal life, and thus access to this knowledge must be carefully managed.
title: Shincheonji Church of Jesus

summary: This reproducibility archive accompanies Marco Mantovanelli's A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws. It contains the manuscript PDF, complete LaTeX source, six vector figures, independent verification programs, figure-generation code, numerical reports, and sampled figure data. The paper studies Q(n) = Q(n - Q(n-1)) + Q(n - Q(n-2)) - (-1)^n for n >= 8, with the seven prescribed initial values (1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5). A causal binary-word construction proves global existence and an exact factorization into three signed excursions. Their uniformly convergent Gaussian profiles explain three limiting sign transitions per standard dyadic block and a sharp normalized error envelope of approximately 0.067088003576. The paper also proves exact finite transition locations, an ordered frequency factorization, a shifted 2-adic valuation law on pure dyadic value blocks, and a summatory asymptotic with an explicit continuous periodic term. The archived verification compares all 33,554,432 directly computed terms with an independent word reconstruction, checks complete frequency blocks through level 21, and verifies the exact summatory identity at every even cutoff from 8 through 33,554,432. Separate programs audit the word maps, finite transitions, and exact two-head identities. These computations supplement the general proofs in the manuscript. The original perturbation, OEIS A394051, is discussed for comparison.
title: A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws (Reproducibility Archive)

summary: This archive contains supplementary code, data, finite certificates, and reproduction instructions for “Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces” by Makoto Ozawa (arXiv:2605.25322). This release accompanies the 41-page revision prepared in October 2026 and preserves all files from the two supplementary archives published in the previous Zenodo version. The computations concern embedded polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves. Polygons are identified under translations, proper cubic rotations, cyclic changes of starting point, and reversal of traversal; spatial reflections are retained. The archive includes the original implementations, seed files, search summaries, and explicit merge-path certificates, together with the complete minimal-layer material for the figure-eight knot and the knot 6_3. For the figure-eight knot, four minimal-layer components at length 30 merge into one component at cap 32. For 6_3, twelve minimal-layer components at length 40 merge into two mirror-related branches at cap 42 and one branch at cap 44. These statements concern the branches originating in the minimal layers, rather than an enumeration of every component at higher caps. The new trefoil supplement certifies six nonminimal components born at length 26 for a fixed chirality. Five first meet the minimal layer at cap 28, whereas a 20-state component first meets it at cap 30. The archive supplies closed component lists, capped-component separation certificates, explicit connecting paths, verification programs, and audit logs. The individual component and exact merge-height certificates do not assume exhaustion of the length-26 population; exhaustiveness at that level remains conditional on the reported literature population. The trefoil material also includes the actual BFACF path used in Figure 2: 47 configurations connected by 46 moves, with maximum length 30. All coordinates, the complete sequence of configurations, figure-generation code, and independent transition checks are provided. Additional checks verify coordinate spans of the specified trefoil components and singleton capped components for supplied 48-edge representatives of 8_3 and 8_7, including an improper spatial symmetry of the 8_3 representative. The release includes the corresponding manuscript source and figures, current documentation, checksums, provenance records, and a verification runner. Historical manuscripts are retained separately in the legacy directory; the current manuscript source is arxiv_revision/main.tex. The documentation distinguishes certified finite results from conditional completeness statements and open questions concerning eventual connectivity, Gordian configurations, and unbounded strong local-minimum birth levels. Requirements: Python 3 for the verification scripts and a C++17 compiler for the large capped-component audits. Regenerating the trefoil figures additionally requires NumPy and Matplotlib. Detailed commands and the scope of each verification are given in the included README files.
title: Supplementary code and data for "Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces"

summary: rnaseq-flow offline Singularity container bundle (v1.7.0) A complete set of Singularity/Apptainer container images for running the rnaseq-flow bulk RNA-seq pipeline on systems with no internet access — Trusted Research Environments, secure enclaves, and air-gapped HPC. Usage tar -xf rnaseq-flow-1.7.0-singularity.tar export NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR=$PWD/singularity-1.7.0 nextflow run main.nf -c $NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR/tre.config -profile tre,<your-executor-profile> --input samplesheet.csv --aligner star ... summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. Author: Lisa Doumbouya   Research programme: Harmonic Physics Research Programme keywords: String theory; Sine-Gordon equation; Pohlmeyer reduction; Classical strings; Phase dynamics; Coupled phase fields; Relative phase; Cosine interaction; Breather solutions; Solitons; Nonlinear dynamics; Expansion and contraction; Computational reproducibility; Phase theory; Harmonic Physics
title: String Theory and Phase Dynamics: An Exact Conditional Sine-Gordon Correspondence

summary: This paper offers a candidate descriptive model based on the author’s retrospective account of internal agent-like experience during a past period of social isolation, emotional distress and perceived high cognitive load. It is a non-clinical reconstruction, not a technique, treatment or recommendation. No contemporaneous physiological, behavioral or neuroimaging measurements were recorded. The Opposition–Load–Coupling vocabulary organizes reported phases of self-talk, opposition, felt load, perceived coupling, autonomy, boundary degradation and disengagement. These are reported experiences and interpretive constructs, not demonstrated causal mechanisms. Claimed benefits and harms are unmeasured first-person reports. The Shared Value Anchor is an untested candidate predictor, not an established stabilizer or necessary condition. The case does not establish whether value conflict preceded initial boundary degradation or distinguish the proposal from a simpler load-based account. The model is situated alongside dialogical-self, Internal Family Systems, predictive-processing, imaginary-companion, writer-agency and tulpa literature. Any incremental contribution lies in the proposed coupling vocabulary and separately testable value-anchor hypothesis, not in discovering internal multiplicity or proving a new mechanism. Safety: do not intentionally induce or replicate the conditions described. This is the author’s own past experience, published at the author’s direction; no formal ethics approval or exemption is claimed. Version 4 incorporates author-adopted revisions following advisory and changed-text checks, including prior-involved AI reviewers. Those checks are not independent peer review, clinical validation or evidence of effectiveness.

summary: Four-dimensional beam-matrix reconstruction from quadrupole scans is the standard way to mea- sure cross-plane coupling and the intrinsic emittances that a decoupling section can recover. We show that a scan of a single thin quadrupole, normal or skew and placed anywhere in a linear lattice, determines at most nine of the ten beam-matrix parameters for any number of settings, because each measured second moment is quadratic in the quadrupole strength. The unmeasured direction lies in the x–y cross block and has a closed form in terms of the transfer matrices; for a quadrupole followed by a drift of length L its nonzero entries are Wxpy = Wpxy = 1 and Wpxpy = −2/L. Both projected emittances are therefore measured, but the beam matrices consistent with the data form a line segment along which the smaller intrinsic emittance ranges from zero to slightly above its true value, so a single-knob scan gives only an upper bound on it. A thick quadrupole restores the miss- ing direction only weakly, its singular value scaling approximately as the sixth power of the magnet length. Scanning two independently powered quadrupoles of any type makes the reconstruction well posed without additional hardware.
title: Single-knob quadrupole scans do not determine the intrinsic emittances

summary: Description This dataset accompanies a comparative evolutionary-genomics study of ancestral cytosine substitution patterns across human, chimpanzee, bonobo and gorilla lineages. Using hg38-centered UCSC multiz primate alignments and a seven-species phylogenetic framework, we reconstructed ancestral nucleotide states and quantified cytosine substitutions across all 22 human autosomes. The analysis examined CG, CHG and CHH sequence contexts, 256 strand-canonicalized ancestral 5-mer motifs, and lineage-specific substitution patterns. The deposited files include: Chromosome-level ancestral-site datasets at a minimum ancestral-state posterior probability of 0.95. Chromosome-specific 5-mer substitution summaries and quality-control records. Genome-wide cytosine substitution frequencies and context-enrichment ratios. Chromosome-bootstrap uncertainty estimates and cross-lineage motif comparisons. Statistical analyses of lineage-specific motif deviations, including simultaneous confidence intervals. Leave-one-autosome-out predictive comparisons of ancestral 3-mer and 5-mer sequence context. Frozen methodology documentation, validation records, checksums and the fixed seven-species phylogenetic tree. The dataset supports independent examination and downstream reanalysis of the reported numerical findings. Data provenance: UCSC Genome Browser hg38-centered 30-primate multiz alignments, restricted to seven primate species. Computational methods: IQ-TREE 2.3.6 ancestral-state reconstruction under GTR+F+G4, followed by custom Python-based sequence-context and statistical analyses. Limitations: The archive contains processed ancestral-site data and numerical outputs, not the original complete multiple-sequence alignments. It does not contain ancestral DNA methylation measurements, direct estimates of net CpG gain or loss, or calibrated mutation rates. Associated code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23425960 Archive organization: This dataset is distributed across two Zenodo records. This record contains Part 1 of 2. Part 2 is available at https://zenodo.org/records/23442145 . Both parts are required to reconstruct the complete archive. Download all files from both records and follow the instructions in RECONSTRUCTION.txt to assemble and verify the dataset.
title: Ancestral Cytosine Sequence-Context Substitution Data Across Four Hominid Lineages: A 22-Autosome Comparative Analysis. Part 1

summary: The rapid expansion of the gig economy, facilitated by digital talent platforms, has fundamentally reconfigured the nature of work, employment relationships, and organizational structures. This paradigm shift from stable, long-term employment to a fluid workforce of contractors, freelancers, and project-based talent presents profound challenges to conventional leadership theories and practices. Traditional models, predicated on hierarchical authority, stable organizational boundaries, and enduring psychological contracts, are proving increasingly inadequate for orchestrating a workforce characterized by autonomy, transience, and distributed networks. This paper conducts a critical review of existing leadership literature—including transformational, adaptive, and emerging platform leadership theories—assessing their applicability and limitations in the gig context. Synthesizing insights from organizational behavior, strategic management, and technology studies, we propose a novel integrated framework: the Fluid Leadership Ecosystem (FLE) Model. The FLE model conceptualizes leadership not as a function of individual authority but as the cultivation of a dynamic ecosystem across three core dimensions: Relational Architecture, Algorithmic Stewardship, and Capability Cultivation. We argue that effective leadership in this new era requires designing trust-enabling infrastructures, ensuring human-centric governance of management algorithms, and fostering portable skill development for a transient workforce. This paper introduces novel theoretical perspectives, including temporal leadership dynamics, polycontextual leadership challenges, and the concept of reverse leadership flows from workers to platforms. By presenting a comprehensive model supported by data visualizations and identifying avenues for empirical validation, this research offers a forward-looking agenda for both scholars and practitioners navigating the complexities of leadership in the 21st-century workforce.
title: The Gig Economy and Talent Platforms: New Models of Leadership for Managing a Fluid Workforce

summary: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?
title: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. summary: DARE TO DRAW YOUR SWORD AGAINST DESTINY is a long-form philosophical poem exploring the courage of individuals who dare to confront fate, even when victory is uncertain and the path ahead remains unknown. At its heart lies a simple yet powerful conviction: heroism is not defined solely by triumph, but by the willingness to stand against overwhelming circumstances without surrendering one’s dignity, conscience, or hope. Through poetic reflections on solitude, struggle, resilience, freedom, and the human spirit, this work portrays the act of drawing one’s sword against destiny as a symbol of existential courage rather than violence. The poem celebrates not only those who overcome adversity, but also those who continue forward despite failure, uncertainty, and the absence of recognition. Beyond its heroic imagery, the work embraces a deeper philosophy: true strength is not merely the power to resist, but also the capacity to protect, to remain compassionate, and to preserve warmth in a world that can often be unforgiving. Created within the imaginative framework of the White Rainbow Era, this literary work reflects the principle of Strength-Grounded Warmth—a vision of kindness supported by courage, boundaries, responsibility, and inner conviction. Ultimately, DARE TO DRAW YOUR SWORD AGAINST DESTINY offers a tribute to every ordinary person who has ever faced an extraordinary struggle. Its central message is timeless: To dare to challenge destiny is already an act of heroism. Victory may belong to circumstance, but courage belongs to the one who dares.
title: ⚔️ English Title DARE TO DRAW YOUR SWORD AGAINST DESTINY

summary: Large language models often penalize multilingual users through hidden 'tokenizer taxes' caused by subword fragmentation. Geographic proper nouns offer a controlled stress case for this distributional asymmetry, as they are standardized, cross-linguistically available entities whose orthographic forms frequently mismatch tokenizer training distributions. We introduce the Cross-Linguistic Orthographic Uniqueness Score (CLOUS), a character-level metric based on Shannon surprisal that quantifies the orthographic rarity of localized country names. We evaluate CLOUS on a controlled corpus of 249 ISO-registered country names; generalization to other geographic entity types remains future work. We evaluate CLOUS against tokenization fertility for six production tokenizers spanning three algorithm families across eleven languages and seven script families. Using Spearman rank correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, CLOUS shows significant associative strength with fertility in 61 of 65 valid language-tokenizer combinations. As a screening tool for high-fragmentation entities, CLOUS achieves ROC-AUC = 0.850 and F1 = 0.740, correctly identifying approximately three-quarters of the highest-fragmentation entities from orthographic properties alone. We further show that CLOUS correlates with fertility more strongly than length-based baselines across all evaluated scripts, and outperforms a character bigram surprisal model in 69.2% of tested combinations, particularly for logographic, syllabic, and Latin scripts. Conversely, the bigram baseline proves superior for morphophonologically complex scripts like Arabic and Devanagari, indicating that tokenizer fragmentation is driven by local orthographic context in some scripts and absolute character rarity in others. Script family appears to be the primary driver of CLOUS-fertility correlation strength, with effect sizes ranging from modest for Latin-script languages ) to large for non-Latin scripts (   up to 0.686 for Japanese). These findings suggest that CLOUS may be useful as a lightweight pre-tokenization diagnostic for multilingual NLP pipelines.
title: Estimating Cross-Lingual Tokenization Fragmentation Risk: A Frequency-Based Uniqueness Score for Geographic Entities

summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-three entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

summary: A harness wraps one or more generators (language models, other neural models, programs or people) with a symbolic layer: a rule set and, optionally, a knowledge store. A checker evaluates each candidate output against the rules and returns a verdict and the violated rules. A release gate lets the output, or part of it, leave only when it passes or under an exception policy, fixed in advance or chosen per request. That is the minimal core. Optional modules, used alone or in any combination, extend it. Rules may filter inputs, decoding, finished outputs, agent actions before execution, and outputs already delivered. A failing output may be repaired by a minimal symbolic change, or revised under a budget the generator cannot alter, with the passing part released under caveats. A passing output may carry a receipt tied to the state it was checked against, so that a later change re-checks affected outputs and supersedes a receipt only when its verdict changes (or, optionally, when the facts it records change). The rule set may improve from evidence, each change held inactive until it passes a gate that can refuse unapproved weakening and require independent approval. Further modules separate claims from outcomes, count correlated sources once, re-extract rendered prose, replay decisions, accept statements by cost, add human review, and turn the harness's verdicts, repairs and revisions into training signals. Outputs may also be read into typed records before checking, with size caps and a per-rule estimate of evaluation work, or a step counter, so that each check made by a rule whose work can be estimated or counted is bounded in advance, and a request may bring rules of its own, written by the generator or another source and admitted only when they cannot relax the rules in force. Knowledge and policy changes can then be made in rules instead of model weights, and any fine-tuning that remains needs less manual labelling.
title: Rule-Gated Generation: A Harness That Filters, Repairs, Certifies and Re-Checks Machine-Generated Output and Improves Its Own Rules Under a Gate

summary: Who supplies, controls and sustains the services needed to inspect and continue AI-assisted research? This article approaches that question through institutional economics and an evolutionary analogy grounded in market competition. It compares targeted evidence with maintained support against fuller research histories with curated access and support. Three activities organize the comparison: scrutiny of a specified claim, reprocessing retained material under a new question, and continuation of unfinished inquiry. A worked access-review example identifies the rights, expertise, labour and resources required, including conditions under which targeted provision is preferable. Market competition supplies the foundational analogy for evolutionary pressure. Repeated decisions about submissions, paid services, funding and volunteer labour can change which research capabilities remain available and which practices spread. Because competing venues can share infrastructure, institutions and their supporting facilities may follow different paths. The article distinguishes internal revision, transmission and differential support, and separates institutional persistence from scientific validity. JOSS and Rainfall Rescue illustrate particular activities and relationships without establishing the comparative benefits of fuller AI histories. The analysis also addresses selective recording, behaviour under scrutiny, unequal burdens and self-selection. Its contribution connects institutional design to the continuing work and support needed to make research records usable.
title: AI Research and the Evolution of Scholarly Institutions

summary: This repository provides the official reproduction software, numerical simulation datasets, and empirical input fixtures for the manuscript: Song, X., Xu, H., & Bai, Y. (2026). Width Oscillations Regulate Event-Driven Bank Collapse and Point-Bar Growth in Transitional Meanders. Journal of Geophysical Research: Earth Surface. ( Under Review ) ABSTRACT Alluvial meanders dynamically adjust their planform and channel geometry, yet classical meander theory assumes a spatially uniform, constant channel width and continuous bank retreat, failing to capture episodic bank collapse and non-uniform width adjustments in transitional meandering rivers. Situated along the geomorphic continuum between single-thread and wandering streams, transitional meanders exhibit pronounced spatial width variations that break cross-sectional symmetry. Here, we develop a physically closed, reduced-complexity morphodynamic framework coupling a three-parameter asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional Reynolds-averaged flow equations, continuous basal toe scour with transient pore-water suction, threshold-governed cantilever limit equilibrium, and a mass-conserving sediment partition driving inner point-bar progradation. The formulation demonstrates that the spatial phase relationship between channel width oscillations and centerline curvature steers the spatial displacement of outer-bank shear stress hotspots: channel constriction upstream of the bend apex amplifies cutbank shear stress, whereas channel expansion decelerates flow and promotes point-bar accretion. Discrete slump-block deposits provide self-adaptive hydraulic shielding that stabilizes the toe and regulates decadal channel relaxation. Hindcasting the 40-year morphodynamic evolution of the transitional Powder River, Montana, across 34 monumented cross sections reproduces post-flood channel widening and subsequent multi-decadal recovery narrowing across 228 discrete collapse events, while in the limit of uniform width the model recovers classical constant-width meander theory with first-order convergence along the meandering Juruá River. Global parameter sweeps quantitatively encompass observed erosion-to-accretion balance ratios across 84 worldwide natural rivers, providing a multiscale morphodynamic framework that links event-scale geotechnical failure to multi-decadal width evolution in alluvial channels. summary: Decentralized multi-robot shape formation in GPS-denied environments is important for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Conventional consensus-based formation controllers can violate safe separation, oscillate, or stall when communication degrades, sensors are noisy, or an agent drops out. This paper proposes a resilient decentralized controller that combines Huber-weighted consensus and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) state estimation with a Dual-Layer Artificial Potential Field (APF) safety barrier. The first layer adds an anti-symmetric lateral deflection to resolve head-on encounters between peers; the second applies a normal-plus-tangential circulation field around static obstacles. The framework is evaluated on five simulated nonholonomic differential-drive robots in Gazebo Harmonic (ROS 2 Jazzy). Three runs are compared: a linear consensus baseline, the same baseline under faults (15% packet loss, 50-150 ms delay, σ = 0.18 m sensor noise, and a mid-run agent blackout), and the proposed controller under the same faults. The fault-free baseline reached the pentagon fastest (0.0156 m final RMS error) but its minimum separation fell to 0.3918 m, with 31 logged violations of the 0.50 m margin. Under faults the baseline reached 0.0546 m with 5 violations (minimum 0.4833 m). The proposed controller recorded no violations, kept a minimum separation of 0.6757 m, and reached 0.0368 m final error, at the cost of slower convergence (about 21 s versus about 12-15 s). Results are from single simulation runs, and the safety barrier is empirical rather than formally guaranteed.
title: Resilient Decentralized Shape Formation of Multi-Robot Swarms Under Adversarial Real-World Faults in High-Complexity Disaster Environments

summary: Popper’s (1983, 2002) philosophy of science has enjoyed something of a renaissance in the wake of the replication crisis, offering a philosophical basis for the ensuing science reform movement. However, adherence to Popper’s approach may also be at least partly responsible for the sense of “crisis” that has developed following multiple unexpected replication failures. In this article, I contrast Popper’s approach with that of Lakatos (1978) as well as with a related but problematic approach called naïve methodological falsificationism (NMF; Lakatos, 1978). The Popperian approach is powerful because it is based on logical refutations, but its theories are noncausal and, therefore, potentially lacking in scientific value. In contrast, the Lakatosian approach considers causal theories, but it concedes that these theories are not logically refutable. Finally, NMF represents a hybrid approach that subjects Lakatosian causal theories to Popperian logical refutations. However, its tactic of temporarily accepting a ceteris paribus clause during theory testing may be viewed as scientifically inappropriate, epistemically inconsistent, and “completely redundant” (Lakatos, 1978, p. 40). I conclude that the replication “crisis” makes the most sense in the context of the Popperian and NMF approaches because it is only in these two approaches that the failure to replicate a previously corroborated theory represents a logical refutation of that theory. In contrast, such replication failures are less problematic in the Lakatosian approach because they do not logically refute theories. Indeed, in the Lakatosian approach, replication failures can be temporarily ignored or used to motivate theory development.
title: The replication crisis is less of a "crisis" in Lakatos' philosophy of science than it is in Popper's.

summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.
title: Synthesis and Verification of Transformer Programs

summary: Image harmonization methods adjust the colour and lighting of an object pasted into a photograph so that it looks native to its new scene, and they are ranked by average error on one benchmark whose test images are real photographs with one object recoloured. One photograph can yield several such test images, and the benchmark promises that no photograph appears in both the training and the test split. We find that 1,399 photographs do, and the composites built on them are a quarter of the test set. Duplicate checks over file names or bytes miss this, because every composite is a different file. On that quarter the three methods we score end to end read two to five times lower error than on the rest, but most of the gap is composition rather than the sharing: the shared composites come almost entirely from one of the benchmark's four source collections, and inside that collection the gap falls to about one and a half times. An official score is therefore an average over two populations, mixed in a proportion the benchmark does not report. We release a test list of 5,581 composites whose construction identities do not appear in training, with four near-duplicate pairs disclosed rather than removed, adoptable without retraining at the price of one rescore per checkpoint. We leave open whether the sharing itself changes what a model learns. Contents of this record. The paper, the supplement, the LaTeX source of both, the record metadata and the licence statement. The identity matcher, the composite-locality and sensitivity checks, the CPU tests, the official iHarmony4 lists and the corrected test list are released under the MIT license at https://github.com/Buljic/only-means-only . What this record does not contain. No dataset, no images, no masks, no model checkpoints and no third-party baseline code or weights; those are described and cited by the paper and remain under their own terms. This is a preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
title: Only Means Only: what a harmonization benchmark score averages over

summary: The dataset, prepared by Patriotisk Selskab for Bikubenfonden and Høbbet A/S, presents spatially distributed soil analysis conducted in 2024. It includes measurements of soil texture (clay content), organic matter (humus content), soil acidity (reaction number, Rt), and nutrient indicators for phosphorus (Pt), potassium (Kt) and magnesium (Mgt). The results are presented through georeferenced sampling locations, field-level maps and thematic maps illustrating spatial variations in soil properties and nutrient levels. The dataset provides baseline information on soil conditions across the investigated areas and can support assessments of soil fertility, vegetation development, habitat restoration and future land management.
title: Soil Analyses of Svanninge Bjerge and Høbbet – Soil Properties and Nutrient Distribution (2024)

summary: Metascience uses a scientific approach to understand and improve science. Critical metascience takes a step back to question metascience’s common assumptions, methods, problems, and solutions. In this article, I aim to raise the profile of critical metascience and offer a rationale for viewing it as a distinct area of multidisciplinary inquiry. I define critical metascience, explain why it is important, and address some potential concerns about it. I also consider some emerging themes in the area and evaluate its potential relationships with metascience. I conclude that there needs to be greater recognition of critical metascience and greater interaction between metascience and critical metascience in order to improve metascience’s objectivity and approach.
title: What is critical metascience and why is it important?

summary: Loss and phase jitter told apart from squeezing pairs at several pump levels, resonances split by backscattering, a wrong error bar of the transmission fit fixed, a faster photonic-molecule model, two test tolerances tied to their floating-point limits, and a third tutorial. Fixed fit_resonance_transmission(..., branch=...) gave wrong error bars for kappa_ex_hz and kappa_0_hz . The derivative of the escape efficiency with respect to the dip depth D, which is -1 / (4 sqrt(1 - D)) on the over-coupled branch and +1 / (4 sqrt(1 - D)) on the under-coupled one, had the opposite sign on both, which flipped the term that carries the (strong, negative) correlation of the linewidth and the depth. Over-coupled ring ( kappa = 100 MHz , eta = 0.8 , 121 points over +/- 300 MHz, 1 % noise): kappa_0_hz_sigma 0.325 MHz -> 0.171 MHz (Monte Carlo scatter of 400 scans: 0.166 MHz), kappa_ex_hz_sigma 0.768 MHz -> 0.946 MHz (scatter 0.900 MHz). Under-coupled ring ( eta = 0.3 ): kappa_ex_hz_sigma 0.427 MHz -> 0.197 MHz (scatter 0.189 MHz), kappa_0_hz_sigma 0.452 MHz -> 0.735 MHz (scatter 0.695 MHz). The fitted values, kappa_hz , eta_esc and eta_sigma were right and are unchanged. Test: test_kappa_ex_and_kappa_0_error_bars . Added fit_squeezing_pairs(sq_db, anti_db, sigma_db, sigma_anti_db=None, fit_jitter=True, dark_noise=0, dark_in_reference=False) : the total efficiency and the local-oscillator phase jitter shared by squeezed / antisqueezed pairs measured at several pump levels, with error bars, each pair's source level, and a chi-square check. One pair cannot separate loss from jitter ( infer_source needs the jitter given); several pairs can, because loss pulls every pair toward shot noise by the same fraction while jitter mixes in a part of the antisqueezing, which grows with the pump. Model: a pure source per pair (no law between pump power and gain assumed), the jitter law of phase_noise_variance , then the efficiency and a stated dark noise as in detected_variance . Checked against the package's own forward path (the output of single_mode_parametric behind an escape efficiency, at three analysis frequencies, is exactly such a source: efficiency to 1e-8, jitter to a relative 1e-6), against infer_source for one pair without jitter (relative 1e-10), and by 150 seeded noisy sets (scatter 0.75 to 1.3 times the error bars). The analysis follows how experiments describe loss and jitter, for example B. Shajilal et al., arXiv:2211.06632 (2022), who model their squeezing and antisqueezing against pump power with a total efficiency and a jitter angle. README example 24. split_transmission(...) and fit_split_resonance(f_hz, transmission, sigma, fit_slope=False) : a through-port dip split into a doublet by backscattering, the coupled-mode model of the clockwise and counterclockwise modes of T. J. Kippenberg, S. M. Spillane and K. J. Vahala, Opt. Lett. 27, 1669 (2002). Returns the linewidth of each standing-wave mode, the escape efficiency, the splitting and the center with error bars, for the under- and the over-coupled regime (a resolved doublet is not symmetric under eta -> 1 - eta , so a regime that does not fit is reported as such), and their chi-square difference. The transmission is derived in the sqzcomb.resonance docstring and checked against the drift matrix of photonic_molecule (relative 1e-13 at 140 points), noise-free recovery (1e-8) and 40 seeded noisy scans. fit_resonance_transmission now names it when it refuses a doublet. README example 25. New test files tests/test_squeezing_pairs.py (9 tests), tests/test_split_resonance.py (9) and tests/test_audit_017.py (6), and one more test in tests/test_tutorials.py . Changed through_transmission (and the new split_transmission ) refuse a center frequency or baseline that is not finite (it returned an all-NaN curve). output_variance_ports is split into its input checks, the resolvent and the evaluation (private helpers); its operations and results are unchanged. molecule_spectra_model u
title: sqzcomb: Lugiato-Lefever steady states and detected squeezing spectra for Kerr microcombs

summary: This release contains the Python code, synthetic numerical data, figure-generation scripts, verification routines and supporting documentation accompanying "Tempered fractional hypercomplex fuzzy neural networks: μ-pseudo almost automorphic solutions and global exponential attraction." The package includes quaternion and octonion examples, structured real-component controls, compensated-gain comparisons and a manufactured periodic whole-line benchmark.
